text: This update focuses on the four Route 2 carrier and target combinations. Each sequence starts from the same Strategy F Run 21 save and carries the damage state forward through FR76 Runs 22–25.

text: Two target rules crossed with two Wave B carrier periods
textPreview: Two target rules crossed with two Wave B carrier periods

name: methods-footer-note
text: Methods 3–4 use precomputed capacity-proxy targets that vary with intensity. The schedule is independent of the preceding 3DEC response.
textPreview: Methods 3–4 use precomputed capacity-proxy targets that vary with intensity. The schedule is independent of the preceding 3DEC response.

text: Wave A is common to all four methods and targets scale × Sd(T1), where T1 is about 0.1119 s. Methods 1 and 2 use fixed target points at T1 and Teff, with Teff about 0.2414 s. Methods 3 and 4 use the precomputed capacity-proxy target d* and T* for each intensity. Method 1 carries Wave B at Teff; Method 2 uses the FR76 predominant period Tp = 0.260 s; Method 3 carries Wave B at T*; Method 4 uses Tp. The adaptive schedule is precomputed and independent of the preceding 3DEC response.

name: fit-provisional-note
text: All 16 spectral fits missed the 2% convergence tolerance. Treat these response rankings as provisional.
textPreview: All 16 spectral fits missed the 2% convergence tolerance. Treat these response rankings as provisional.

alt: Four-method comparison of peak relative out-of-plane displacement, peak base shear, and mean spectral target error. Legends read Method 1 through Method 4.

text: Metrics use the three experimental comparisons available for US-1 Test 9, Runs 22–24. Method 2 has the lowest mean absolute percentage error in peak relative OOP displacement at 17.1%. Method 1 has the lowest mean absolute percentage error in peak base shear at 9.3%. Run 25 is shown for the model sequence only because no US-1 Test 9 experiment exists for that run. The four methods used the common Strategy F Run 21 starting state. All 16 signal fits report fit_converged=False at the 2% tolerance, so the method ranking is preliminary.

text: Method 1 uses the per-method plot generated from the project copy of Claude outputs/baseshear_exp_from_model.py. The script sums tributary masses at sensors 15–17 using ρ = 1,619 kg/m³ and applies MASS_SCALE = 2.317348 to both the model and experimental sides. The source figure also retains US-2 Test 12 and the support reaction traces. The reported mean base-shear peak error is the mean absolute percentage error over the three available US-1 Test 9 comparisons, Runs 22–24.

text: Experimental points are read from Claude outputs/exp_Test9_incl_tilt.csv, column resid_tilt_y_deg: Run 21 = 2.756°, Run 22 = 2.529°, Run 23 = 2.3965°, and Run 24 = 6.035°. Run 24 is +3.279° relative to Run 21. The within-shaking inclinometers clip near ±25.75°; this figure therefore uses settled residuals. No matched model instrument-point tilt series is presented. The current local chord-angle proxy is deliberately excluded from this experimental comparison.

name: summary-scope-note
text: Runs 22–24 have US-1 comparisons. Run 25 is model-only. All methods start from Strategy F Run 21.
textPreview: Runs 22–24 have US-1 comparisons. Run 25 is model-only. All methods start from Strategy F Run 21.

text: The mean error metrics compare Methods 1–4 against US-1 Test 9 for Runs 22–24. Method 2 gives the lowest mean absolute OOP displacement error at 17.1%; Method 1 gives the lowest mean absolute base-shear peak error at 9.3%. These four runs do not identify one overall winner. All spectral calibration fits missed the 2% convergence tolerance, so first improve the joint two-wave fit. Then generate a model tilt measure at the actual inclinometer location and compare settled residuals before selecting a method.
